channel.title: Dodge recalls — Car Recall Tracker
channel.description: NHTSA vehicle safety recalls explained in plain English.

item.title: Dodge Durango Rear Spoiler Detachment Risk
item.description: On some Dodge Durango vehicles, the rear spoiler may not line up correctly with the roof. Because of this, the spoiler can get damaged when the liftgate is opened or closed. A damaged spoiler could eventually come loose from the vehicle. A spoiler that falls off onto the road creates a hazard for other drivers, which raises the risk of a crash.

item.title: Dodge Hornet, Alfa Romeo Tonale Seat Belts May Not Retract
item.description: On these Dodge Hornet and Alfa Romeo Tonale vehicles, the rear seat belts next to the windows can become twisted. When that happens, the belt may not pull back in the way it should. A belt that does not retract properly may not hold an occupant in place the way it is meant to. Dealers will replace the retractors, the parts that wind the belt in and out, at no cost to the owner.

item.title: Jeep Wagoneer S and Dodge Charger EV display may fail
item.description: Chrysler is recalling certain Jeep Wagoneer S and Dodge Charger electric vehicles. A software problem can make the display in front of the driver stop working, so the information it normally shows is not available. Because of this, these vehicles do not meet several federal safety standards, covering vehicle lamps, stability control, brakes, the tire pressure monitoring system and occupant crash protection.

item.title: Wheelchair Restraints in Various Vehicles May Not Lock
item.description: Certain vehicles equipped with QRT-Deluxe or QRT-Max wheelchair restraints may have retractors that fail to lock. If the retractor does not lock, a wheelchair inside the vehicle may not be properly secured.

item.title: Dodge Charger EV, Jeep Wagoneer S May Roll Away
item.description: On these Dodge Charger and Jeep Wagoneer S electric vehicles, an incorrectly installed spring may cause the vehicle to lose its 'Park' function when the gear selector is placed in Park, which can lead to the vehicle rolling away.

item.title: Ram ProMaster, Dodge Journey backup camera may fail
item.description: Cracks can develop in a microprocessor used by the rearview camera on these vehicles. When that happens, the camera's image may not display properly on the screen, so these vehicles do not meet the federal safety standard for rear visibility. Dealers will replace the rearview camera at no charge, though the replacement parts are not yet available. Interim letters warning owners of the issue were mailed starting September 30, 2025, and a second letter announcing the final remedy is expected around July 2026.

item.title: Dodge Charger EV may not sound pedestrian warning
item.description: These Dodge Charger electric cars are supposed to make sound on the outside so people nearby can hear them coming. On the recalled vehicles, the amplifier that creates that sound may be missing its software. Without that software, the amplifier may not put out any exterior sound at all, including the alert meant to warn pedestrians. Because of this, the vehicles do not meet the federal rule setting a minimum sound requirement for electric and hybrid vehicles.

item.title: Dodge Hornet Rearview Camera Display Failure
item.description: In some Dodge Hornet vehicles, the display screen may not show the rearview camera image. Without that image, the driver has a reduced view of what's behind the vehicle while backing up. This reduced visibility increases the risk of a crash.

item.title: Jeep Grand Cherokee and Durango Brake Module Fault
item.description: In some Grand Cherokee and Durango SUVs, a malfunction in the antilock brake module can incorrectly turn on the brake lights and disable the antilock brakes and stability control. It may also allow the vehicle to be started and shifted out of Park without the driver pressing the brake pedal.

item.title: Dodge Hornet brake pedal may collapse while driving
item.description: On some 2024-2025 Dodge Hornet and Alfa Romeo Tonale vehicles, the brake pedal may collapse, causing a loss of brake function. Dealers will reinforce the brake pedal arm to fix the problem, free of charge.

item.title: Dodge Charger Rear Seat Back May Not Lock
item.description: In these vehicles, the left rear seat back may not lock into the upright position the way it should. If the seat back does not lock properly, it will not hold as intended if the vehicle is in a crash. Dealers will inspect the seat back's latch and striker and adjust them as needed so the seat locks correctly, at no charge to the owner.

item.title: Dodge Challenger left rear seat back may not lock
item.description: On some 2023 Dodge Challenger cars, the left rear seat back may not lock in its upright position. That means it may not stay firmly in place the way the seat is designed to. Because of this, these cars do not meet the federal safety rule covering seating systems. Dealers will check the latch piece that the seat back catches on and adjust it if needed. Chrysler mailed letters to owners in August 2024.

item.title: Chrysler, Jeep, Ram Rearview Camera May Not Display
item.description: A software issue in the radio can prevent the rearview camera image from displaying on the screen. Because of this, these vehicles do not meet the requirements of the federal safety standard for rear visibility, FMVSS 111. To fix the problem, dealers will update the radio software, or the software update will be delivered over-the-air. This repair is free of charge for owners of the affected vehicles.

item.title: Dodge Durango, Ram Trucks Lose Stability Control
item.description: A software problem in the ABS control module can disable the electronic stability control system on affected Dodge Durango and Ram trucks. Because of this, the vehicles do not meet a federal safety standard for electronic stability control systems.

item.title: Dodge Hornet Label Missing Tire and Rim Size
item.description: The manufacturer label on affected vehicles is missing tire and rim size information. Without this information, a wheel of the wrong size could be installed on the vehicle.

item.title: Chrysler 300 and Dodge Charger Side Airbag Rupture
item.description: The right and left side curtain airbags in these vehicles may rupture. This happens because of a defect in the way the airbag inflator was manufactured. If the inflator ruptures, it can send sharp pieces of metal flying inside the vehicle's cabin. Those metal fragments could strike the driver or any passengers riding inside, and this could result in injury or even death to the people in the vehicle.

item.title: Dodge Hornet tire label lists wrong weight limit
item.description: Chrysler is recalling certain Dodge Hornet vehicles because of wrong information printed on a label. The tire placard is the sticker that lists tire and loading information for the vehicle, and on these cars the maximum vehicle capacity weight shown on it is incorrect. That means the sticker does not meet the federal rule covering tire selection and rims. Dealers will place a corrected overlay label over the tire placard at no charge.

item.title: Chrysler 300 and Dodge Parking Brake Roll-Away Risk
item.description: The parking brake on some Chrysler 300, Dodge Charger, and Dodge Challenger vehicles may not be adjusted correctly. If the parking brake isn't holding properly, the vehicle could roll away on its own. This roll-away risk increases the chance of a crash or injury.

item.title: Dodge Hornet Pedestrian Alert Siren May Fail
item.description: Some Dodge Hornet vehicles may have a pedestrian warning siren that is missing or disconnected. This siren is meant to alert people outside the vehicle when it is in reverse. Because of this issue, the vehicle may fail to sound the alert while backing up.

item.title: Dodge Durango Shifter May Cause Loss Of Power
item.description: On some Durango Pursuit police vehicles with a dashboard-mounted gear shifter, the shifter boot may interfere with the shifter and cause it to slip out of gear while the vehicle is being driven. When this happens, the vehicle can suddenly lose the power that drives the wheels, which increases the risk of a crash.

item.title: Dodge Hornet Loose Cable Can Cause Fire
item.description: Certain Dodge Hornet and Alfa Romeo Tonale plug-in hybrid electric vehicles may have a 12-volt battery positive cable or a high voltage connector cable that was not tightened properly. A loose connection like this can overheat, and that overheating can result in a fire while the vehicle is parked or being driven.

item.title: Dodge Durango Rear Spoiler May Detach
item.description: The rear spoiler on some Durango SUVs may not be lined up correctly with the roof. This misalignment can cause the spoiler to get damaged simply from normal use of the liftgate, opening and closing it over time. If the spoiler becomes damaged, it can eventually come loose and detach from the vehicle while driving, leaving a piece of the vehicle in the road for other drivers to encounter.

item.title: Dodge Charger, Durango Shifter May Not Engage Drive
item.description: In some Dodge Charger and Durango vehicles, the shifter assembly was not heat-treated properly. Because of this, the shifter may not fully engage in the 'drive' position. A shifter that is not properly engaged can slip out of drive on its own, causing the vehicle to suddenly lose the power needed to keep moving. This loss of drive power can happen while the vehicle is being driven.

item.title: Chrysler 300, Dodge Challenger, Charger Tire Sensor Failure
item.description: The battery in the tire pressure monitoring sensors may fail early, causing the sensor to stop working. If a warning light is already on because of a failed sensor, it can hide a real low tire pressure problem.

item.title: Dodge Journey Headlamp Reflector Too Dim
item.description: On some 2017-2018 Dodge Journey vehicles, the amber side reflector built into the headlamp may not reflect light brightly enough.

item.title: Chrysler 300, Challenger, Charger TPMS Sensor Failure
item.description: On certain 2022 Dodge Challenger, Dodge Charger, and Chrysler 300 vehicles, the battery inside a tire pressure sensor may fail earlier than it should, which can make the sensor stop working. When a sensor stops working this way, it will not warn the driver if a tire's air pressure gets low. If the tire pressure warning light is already on because of a failed sensor battery, it can also hide a real, separate tire pressure problem from the driver.

item.title: Jeep Grand Cherokee, Dodge Durango Can Roll Away
item.description: Chrysler is recalling certain Jeep Grand Cherokee and Dodge Durango vehicles because a malfunction in the anti-lock brake system module may turn on the brake lights and let the vehicle start and shift out of Park without the brake pedal being pressed. A vehicle that does this can roll away on its own, increasing the risk of a crash without warning, and can injure people outside the vehicle.

item.title: Dodge Durango, Jeep Grand Cherokee Sudden Power Loss
item.description: Chrysler is recalling certain Dodge Durango and Jeep Grand Cherokee vehicles. The exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) valve may stick open. When this happens, the vehicle can unexpectedly lose drive power while being driven.

item.title: Dodge Durango Steering Rack Part May Bind
item.description: In certain Dodge Durango vehicles, a bar inside the steering gear rack may not have been hardened enough during manufacturing. Because it is too soft, this bar can bind, or stick, inside the steering rack. When that happens, the driver may find it difficult to steer the vehicle, or in some cases may lose the ability to steer it at all, which affects control of the vehicle.

item.title: Ram and Durango Stability Warning Light May Fail
item.description: A problem with the computer that controls the anti-lock brakes may prevent the electronic stability control warning light from turning on when it should, under certain conditions. If that warning light fails to turn on during an electronic stability control problem, it increases the risk of a crash. Dealers will update the software in that computer to fix the issue, free of charge.

item.title: Dodge Durango Rear Spoiler May Come Loose
item.description: Some Durango SUVs have a rear spoiler that may not be lined up correctly with the roof. Because of this misalignment, the spoiler can get damaged when the liftgate is opened or closed.

item.title: Dodge Challenger Dash Warning Lights Not Visible
item.description: FCA is recalling certain 2021 Dodge Challenger vehicles because the safety system status indicators in the instrument cluster don't light up brightly enough to be seen in daylight or at night. This means drivers may not get information about the vehicle's safety systems when they need it. Dealers will reprogram the instrument cluster with corrected software to fix the issue.

item.title: Chrysler 300, Challenger, Charger windshields may detach in crash
item.description: During manufacturing, the windshield may not have been properly bonded, or glued, to the vehicle. If the vehicle is involved in a crash, a windshield that isn't properly bonded could come loose and separate from the vehicle. A windshield that detaches during a crash may not provide the protection it's designed to give the occupants inside. This increases the risk of injury to those inside the vehicle.

item.title: Dodge Durango side curtain airbag fastener may be loose
item.description: Chrysler is recalling certain Dodge Durango SUVs. A fastener that holds the side curtain airbag in place may be loose or missing. Dealers will tighten the fastener or replace it if needed.

item.title: Jeep, Ram and Dodge backup camera image stays on screen
item.description: Chrysler is recalling certain Jeep, Ram, Dodge and Chrysler vehicles with 8.4-inch or 12-inch radio screens. A software error can leave the backup camera picture on the screen after the driver has shifted out of reverse. Because of this, the vehicles do not meet the federal safety rule covering rear visibility. Dealers will update the radio display software. Owners can also choose to have the software updated remotely, over the air, instead of visiting a dealer.

item.title: Dodge Charger Backup Camera May Not Show in Stealth Mode
item.description: On certain Dodge Charger Pursuit vehicles, when "stealth mode" is selected, the backup camera image does not display when the vehicle is shifted into reverse.

item.title: Modified Grand Caravan fuel gasket may leak
item.description: On some Vantage-modified Grand Caravan vehicles, the fuel pump gasket may wear out over time and allow fuel to leak. If that fuel leak occurs near a source of ignition, it can increase the risk of a fire.

item.title: Dodge Durango, Jeep Grand Cherokee May Lose Power
item.description: On certain 2019 Jeep Grand Cherokee and Dodge Durango vehicles, the front differential may have gears that were not hardened enough, causing the gear teeth to wear down over time. If both gears wear down enough, power can no longer reach the front wheels from the driveline. This can cause a sudden loss of power while driving, and can also cause the transmission to lose its PARK function when the vehicle is stopped.

item.title: Dodge Grand Caravan rear seat strikers may fail
item.description: Welds on the second-row seat strikers may fail in a front-impact crash, and welds on the third-row seat strikers may fail in a rear-impact crash. In addition, the second-row bench and bucket seats may not hold up to the loads they are required to withstand.

item.title: Dodge Challenger and Charger Front Tire Damage
item.description: Certain Dodge Challenger and Charger vehicles were built with a front wheel and brake package that isn't compatible with the vehicle. This mismatch can allow the front tire to rub against a steering part called the steering knuckle, and that contact can damage the tire.
